# OmniDB Documentation

## Overview

OmniDB is an open source browser-based app designed to access and manage many different Database Management systems, e.g. PostgreSQL, Oracle and MySQL. OmniDB can run either as a desktop app or via browser, combining the flexibility needed for various access paths with a design that puts security first. The backend was fully rewritten from Python/Django to Go in 3.6.x, and the desktop shell is migrating from NW.js to Wails; the old Python-based plugin system (pglogical/BDR/Postgres-XL support) was removed in that rewrite and is not coming back — see the Legacy Features & History page.

---

## Introduction

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/introduction.html

**Description:** Introduction to OmniDB - a browser-based database management tool supporting PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL, and more. Features a unified workspace, background execution of queries and procedures across multiple databases, and encrypted data storage.

**Key Topics:**
- History and origins of OmniDB
- Multi-DBMS support
- Security features
- 2025-2026 revival; backend fully rewritten from Python/Django to Go in 3.6.x

## Legacy Features & History

URL: https://www.omnidb.net/en/legacy_features_and_history.html

**Description:** OmniDB's version timeline, and what happened to its removed Python-based plugin system — including the pglogical, Postgres-BDR and Postgres-XL plugins — the removed PL/pgSQL step debugger, and the removed Advanced Object Search feature, after the 3.6.x rewrite from Python/Django to Go. Links to the original unmaintained repository for anyone who still needs an old release with plugin support.

**Key Topics:**
- Version history (original ASP.NET/C# project → Django → 2025-2026 revival → Go rewrite → Wails migration)
- Why the plugin system, pglogical, Postgres-BDR and Postgres-XL support were removed and are not returning
- Why the PL/pgSQL step debugger was removed (never ported to Go, and fundamentally incompatible with managed/cloud PostgreSQL)
- Why Advanced Object Search was removed (dead code calling functions that no longer existed, never functional since the Go rewrite)
- Where to find old releases (github.com/OmniDB/OmniDB, github.com/OmniDB/plugins)

---
